rationale:
Split into three children along boundaries already present in the supplied proof. The split is verified end to end in Lean (details below).

(A) hausdorff_near_optimal_cover / hausdorffMeasure_exists_cover_tsum_le_add = the existence part of Step 4 (Simon (1), chapter-02.txt lines 366–370). It is a generic statement about Hausdorff measure on any extended metric space. Mathlib states only the sup/inf formula hausdorffMeasure_apply, not this ∃-form, so it is a reusable tool for any covering argument in the chapter.

(B) volume_diameter_bound / volume_closure_le_unitBall_mul_ediam_pow = Step 1 (the elementary volume bound λₘ(closure S) ≤ ωₘ(diam S)ᵐ, replacing Simon's isodiametric step, lines 401–406). It is generic and reusable.

(C) eilenberg_core_finite / eilenberg_hausdorff_upper_integral_of_ne_top = Steps 4–7, i.e. Simon's Theorem 1.9 inequality (proof lines 366–411), under Simon's own hypothesis H^{m+k}(A) < ∞, for Mathlib's unnormalized μH, with the explicit constant ωₘ = λₘ(B₁(0)). It depends on A and B. It is the analytic core and not a restatement of the parent: it has an explicit constant and unnormalized measures, it assumes finiteness, and it does not cover the parent's case H^{m+k}(A) = ∞ with L = 0 and m ≥ 1.

How the parent follows from C. The parent keeps exactly the supplied proof's bookkeeping, i.e. its constant and Steps 2–3.

(P1) Constants. ω := λₘ(B₁(0)) ∈ (0, ∞). For d ∈ ℕ, c_d := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on ℝ^d, μH[d]) ∈ ℝ≥0 \ {0}, and μHE[d] S = c_d·μH[d] S for every S. This holds by definition (rw [Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def]; rfl), and c_d ≠ 0 is Measure.addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero. Set C := ω.toNNReal·c_k/c_{m+k}, which is the supplied proof's constant ωₘc_k/c_{m+k}. Then C·c_{m+k} = ω·c_k and C > 0.

(P2) Case μH[m+k](A) < ∞. Child C gives a Borel g₀; take g := c_k·g₀, which is Borel.
- Pointwise: μHE[k](A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = c_k·μH[k](A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ c_k·g₀(y).
- Integral: ∫g = c_k∫g₀ ≤ c_k·ω·L^m·μH[m+k](A) = (C·L^m)·(c_{m+k}·μH[m+k](A)) = C·L^m·μHE[m+k](A).

(P3) Case μH[m+k](A) = ∞. Then μHE[m+k](A) = ∞, because c_{m+k} ≠ 0.
- If C·L^m ≠ 0, the right side is ∞ and g ≡ ∞ works (the supplied Step 3).
- Otherwise L = 0 and m ≥ 1, because C > 0 and L⁰ = 1. Then f is constant, equal to some y₀ (the supplied Step 2), and the slices are empty for y ≠ y₀. Take g := ∞·1_{y₀}: it is Borel, and ∫g = ∞·λₘ({y₀}) = 0, since points are λₘ-null for m ≥ 1.

There is one reorganisation relative to the supplied proof: when L = 0 and H^{m+k}(A) is finite, the argument goes through child C, which handles L = 0 uniformly. With that, A, B and C together with P1–P3 prove the selected statement by the supplied proof's own arguments. No child solves another DAG node.

subproblems.title: Near-optimal countable δ-covers for Hausdorff measure (Simon Ch. 2, proof of Thm 1.9, choice (1))
subproblems.statement: Let X be an extended metric space with its Borel σ-algebra, d ∈ ℝ, s ⊆ X any set (not necessarily measurable), and r, ε ∈ [0, ∞] with r > 0 and ε ≠ 0. Let μH[d] be Mathlib's unnormalized d-dimensional Hausdorff measure on X: for every set s, μH[d](s) = sup_{ρ>0} inf{ Σ_{n∈ℕ} c_d(tₙ) : s ⊆ ⋃ₙ tₙ, diam tₙ ≤ ρ for all n }, where diam is the extended diameter, c_d(t) = diam(t)^d for t ≠ ∅, and c_d(∅) = 0. If μH[d](s) < ∞, then there is a sequence (tₙ)_{n∈ℕ} of subsets of X with s ⊆ ⋃ₙ tₙ, diam tₙ ≤ r for every n, and Σₙ c_d(tₙ) ≤ μH[d](s) + ε.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ {X : Type} [EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (d : ℝ) (s : Set X) (r ε : ℝ≥0∞), 0 < r → ε ≠ 0 → μH[d] s ≠ ∞ → ∃ t : ℕ → Set X, s ⊆ ⋃ n, t n ∧ (∀ n, Metric.ediam (t n) ≤ r) ∧ ∑' n, ⨆ _ : (t n).Nonempty, Metric.ediam (t n) ^ d ≤ μH[d] s + ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source and role. This is the choice of covers (1) in Simon's proof of Ch. 2, Theorem 1.9 (chapter-02.txt lines 366–370: for each i pick C_{i1}, C_{i2}, … with diam C_{ij} < 1/i, A ⊆ ⋃ⱼ C_{ij} and Σⱼ ω_{m+k}(diam C_{ij}/2)^{m+k} ≤ H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A) + 1/i), i.e. the existence part of Step 4 of the parent proof. It is stated for Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure (cost diam^d, normalizing constant 1), and the δ-content H_δ(s) is replaced by the larger number μH[d](s), which is all the parent uses (its Step 7 only needs H^{m+k}_{1/i}(A) ≤ H^{m+k}(A)). Closedness of the covering sets is not claimed: the parent takes closures of images instead.

Notation. diam T ∈ [0, ∞] is the extended diameter; c_d(T) := diam(T)^d if T ≠ ∅ and c_d(∅) := 0 (in Lean: ⨆ _ : T.Nonempty, Metric.ediam T ^ d). For ρ > 0 let
 I_ρ := inf { Σ_{n∈ℕ} c_d(tₙ) : (tₙ)_{n∈ℕ} subsets of X with s ⊆ ⋃ₙ tₙ and diam tₙ ≤ ρ for every n } ∈ [0, ∞]
(infimum in [0, ∞]; the infimum of the empty family is ∞).

Proof.
1. Formula. Mathlib's Hausdorff measure is the metric outer measure generated by the gauge t ↦ diam(t)^d, and for every set s, measurable or not, μH[d](s) = sup_{ρ>0} I_ρ (Mathlib: MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply; the term of an empty tₙ is a supremum over a false proposition, i.e. 0).
2. Comparison. Because r > 0, the index ρ = r occurs in the supremum of step 1, so I_r ≤ μH[d](s).
3. Strict gap. Since μH[d](s) ≠ ∞ and ε ≠ 0, μH[d](s) < μH[d](s) + ε in [0, ∞]; with step 2, I_r < μH[d](s) + ε.
4. Witness. An infimum strictly below a number b has a member strictly below b. I_r is the triple infimum over a sequence t, over a proof of s ⊆ ⋃ₙ tₙ, and over a proof of ∀ n, diam tₙ ≤ r. Applying this fact to the three infima in step 3 gives a sequence (tₙ) with s ⊆ ⋃ₙ tₙ, diam tₙ ≤ r for every n, and Σₙ c_d(tₙ) < μH[d](s) + ε.
5. Conclusion. This sequence has the three required properties (the last in the weaker form ≤). ∎

Remarks. (i) Both hypotheses are used. r > 0 puts I_r below μH[d](s), and finiteness makes step 3 strict (in [0, ∞], ∞ < ∞ + ε is false). Without finiteness the statement fails: an uncountable set whose points are pairwise at distance 1 has no countable cover by sets of diameter ≤ 1/2. (ii) No measurability of s is used. (iii) d is an arbitrary real number; only the formula of step 1 is used.

Formalization notes. Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply, le_iSup₂_of_le, ENNReal.lt_add_right, simp only [iInf_lt_iff], hsum.le.

theorem Submission.hausdorffMeasure_exists_cover_tsum_le_add : ∀ {X : Type} [EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (d : ℝ) (s : Set X) (r ε : ℝ≥0∞), 0 < r → ε ≠ 0 → μH[d] s ≠ ∞ → ∃ t : ℕ → Set X, s ⊆ ⋃ n, t n ∧ (∀ n, Metric.ediam (t n) ≤ r) ∧ ∑' n, ⨆ _ : (t n).Nonempty, Metric.ediam (t n) ^ d ≤ μH[d] s + ε := by
  intro X _ _ _ d s r ε hr hε hs
  set I : ℝ≥0∞ := ⨅ (t : ℕ → Set X) (_ : s ⊆ ⋃ n, t n) (_ : ∀ n, Metric.ediam (t n) ≤ r),
          ∑' n, ⨆ _ : (t n).Nonempty, Metric.ediam (t n) ^ d with hI
  have hIle : I ≤ μH[d] s := by
    rw [Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply]
    exact le_iSup₂_of_le r hr le_rfl
  have hIlt : I < μH[d] s + ε := lt_of_le_of_lt hIle (ENNReal.lt_add_right hs hε)
  rw [hI] at hIlt
  simp only [iInf_lt_iff] at hIlt
  obtain ⟨t, hst, htr, hsum⟩ := hIlt
  exact ⟨t, hst, htr, hsum.le⟩
proof_key_steps: μH[d](s) = sup_{ρ>0} I_ρ, where I_ρ is the infimum of Σₙ c_d(tₙ) over countable covers of s by sets of diameter ≤ ρ (hausdorffMeasure_apply).
μH[d](s) < ∞ and ε ≠ 0 give I_r < μH[d](s) + ε.
Unfold the triple infimum (iInf_lt_iff) to obtain a cover t with diam tₙ ≤ r and Σₙ c_d(tₙ) < μH[d](s) + ε.

subproblems.title: Lebesgue measure of the closure of a set in ℝᵐ is at most ωₘ(diam)ᵐ
subproblems.statement: For every m ∈ ℕ and every set S ⊆ ℝᵐ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m): λₘ(closure S) ≤ λₘ(B₁(0))·(diam S)ᵐ, where λₘ is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝᵐ, B₁(0) is the open unit ball centred at 0, diam S ∈ [0, ∞] is the extended diameter, and the m-th power is taken in [0, ∞] (x⁰ = 1 for every x; ∞ᵐ = ∞ for m ≥ 1).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (S : Set (Rn m)), volume (closure S) ≤ volume (Metric.ball (0 : Rn m) 1) * Metric.ediam S ^ m
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source and role. This is Step 1 of the parent proof (the elementary volume bound). In Simon's proof of Ch. 2, Theorem 1.9 (chapter-02.txt lines 401–406) the corresponding estimate Lᵐ(f(C_{ij})) ≤ ωₘ(diam f(C_{ij})/2)ᵐ is taken from the isodiametric inequality 2.10. As in the parent, it is replaced here by the cruder inclusion S ⊆ B̄_{diam S}(s₀); only the constant changes, and any constant suffices for the parent. The closure is taken so that the set is Borel (Simon instead uses σ-compactness to see that f(C_{ij}) is Borel, lines 375–377).

Notation. λₘ = volume on ℝᵐ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); ωₘ := λₘ(B₁(0)), B₁(0) the open unit ball; powers are taken in [0, ∞].

Proof.
1. S = ∅. Then closure S = ∅ and λₘ(∅) = 0 ≤ right side.
2. m = 0. ℝ⁰ has exactly one point, the zero vector. So B₁(0) = ℝ⁰ (that point is at distance 0 < 1 from 0), (diam S)⁰ = 1, and the right side is λ₀(ℝ⁰) ≥ λ₀(closure S) by monotonicity. From now on S ≠ ∅ (fix s₀ ∈ S) and m ≥ 1.
3. ωₘ > 0. B₁(0) is a nonempty open set, and Lebesgue measure, an additive Haar measure, is positive on nonempty open sets.
4. diam S = ∞. Then (diam S)ᵐ = ∞ (since m ≥ 1) and ωₘ·∞ = ∞ (since ωₘ ≠ 0); the inequality is trivial.
5. diam S < ∞: inclusion. Then S is bounded. Let D := (diam S).toReal ≥ 0 be its real diameter, so ofReal(D) = diam S. The closure of S is bounded and has the same diameter. For x ∈ closure S, both x and s₀ lie in closure S, so dist(x, s₀) ≤ diam(closure S) = D. Hence closure S ⊆ B̄_D(s₀).
6. diam S < ∞: volume of the ball. λₘ is translation invariant, scales by ρᵐ under x ↦ ρx, and dim ℝᵐ = m, so λₘ(B̄_D(s₀)) = Dᵐ·λₘ(B₁(0)) (Mathlib: MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_closedBall, whose right side is ofReal(D^finrank)·μ(ball 0 1), together with finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Moreover ofReal(Dᵐ) = ofReal(D)ᵐ = (diam S)ᵐ, because D ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pow) and ofReal((diam S).toReal) = diam S since diam S ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
7. Conclusion. By monotonicity and steps 5–6, λₘ(closure S) ≤ λₘ(B̄_D(s₀)) = (diam S)ᵐ·ωₘ = ωₘ·(diam S)ᵐ. ∎

Formalization notes. Set.eq_empty_or_nonempty; for m = 0, Subsingleton.elim x 0 gives Metric.ball (0 : Rn 0) 1 = univ; Metric.measure_ball_pos; ENNReal.top_pow; ENNReal.mul_top; Metric.isBounded_iff_ediam_ne_top; Metric.diam_closure; Metric.dist_le_diam_of_mem; Measure.addHaar_closedBall volume s₀ Metric.diam_nonneg; finrank_euclideanSpace_fin; ENNReal.ofReal_pow; Metric.diam (the toReal of Metric.ediam); ENNReal.ofReal_toReal.

theorem Submission.volume_closure_le_unitBall_mul_ediam_pow : ∀ (m : ℕ) (S : Set (Rn m)), volume (closure S) ≤ volume (Metric.ball (0 : Rn m) 1) * Metric.ediam S ^ m := by
  intro m S
  rcases S.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | ⟨s₀, hs₀⟩
  · simp
  by_cases hm : m = 0
  · subst hm
    have hball : Metric.ball (0 : Rn 0) 1 = univ := by
      ext x; simp [Subsingleton.elim x 0]
    rw [pow_zero, mul_one, hball]
    exact measure_mono (subset_univ _)
  have hω0 : volume (Metric.ball (0 : Rn m) 1) ≠ 0 := (Metric.measure_ball_pos volume (0 : Rn m) one_pos).ne'
  by_cases hD : Metric.ediam S = ∞
  · rw [hD, ENNReal.top_pow hm, ENNReal.mul_top hω0]
    exact le_top
  have hb : Bornology.IsBounded S := Metric.isBounded_iff_ediam_ne_top.2 hD
  have hsub : closure S ⊆ Metric.closedBall s₀ (Metric.diam S) := by
    intro x hx
    rw [Metric.mem_closedBall, ← Metric.diam_closure]
    exact Metric.dist_le_diam_of_mem hb.closure hx (subset_closure hs₀)
  calc volume (closure S) ≤ volume (Metric.closedBall s₀ (Metric.diam S)) := measure_mono hsub
    _ = ENNReal.ofReal (Metric.diam S ^ m) * volume (Metric.ball (0 : Rn m) 1) := by
        rw [Measure.addHaar_closedBall volume s₀ Metric.diam_nonneg, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin]
    _ = volume (Metric.ball (0 : Rn m) 1) * Metric.ediam S ^ m := by
        rw [mul_comm, ENNReal.ofReal_pow Metric.diam_nonneg, Metric.diam, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal hD]
proof_key_steps: Trivial cases: S = ∅; m = 0, where B₁(0) = ℝ⁰ and the power is 1.
m ≥ 1 and diam S = ∞: the right side is ∞ because ωₘ > 0.
Bounded S: closure S ⊆ B̄_{diam S}(s₀) for any s₀ ∈ S, because diam(closure S) = diam S.
λₘ(B̄_D(s₀)) = Dᵐ·ωₘ (addHaar_closedBall, finrank = m) and ofReal(D)ᵐ = (diam S)ᵐ.

subproblems.title: Eilenberg's inequality for unnormalized Hausdorff measure when H^{m+k}(A) < ∞ (Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.9, proof lines 366–411)
subproblems.statement: Let N, m, k ∈ ℕ, let A ⊆ ℝ^N be arbitrary (not necessarily measurable), L ∈ [0, ∞), and f : ℝ^N → ℝᵐ L-Lipschitz (ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)). Let μH[s] be Mathlib's unnormalized s-dimensional Hausdorff (outer) measure on ℝ^N (gauge diam^s; the exponents are the real numbers k and m + k), λₘ = volume on ℝᵐ, and ωₘ := λₘ(B₁(0)) with B₁(0) the open unit ball of ℝᵐ. If μH[m+k](A) < ∞, there is a Borel measurable g : ℝᵐ → [0, ∞] with μH[k](A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g(y) for every y ∈ ℝᵐ and ∫ g dλₘ ≤ ωₘ·L^m·μH[m+k](A).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N m k : ℕ) (A : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (L : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith L f → μH[((m + k : ℕ) : ℝ)] A ≠ ∞ → ∃ g : Rn m → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ (∀ y, μH[(k : ℝ)] (A ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}) ≤ g y) ∧ ∫⁻ y, g y ≤ volume (Metric.ball (0 : Rn m) 1) * (L : ℝ≥0∞) ^ m * μH[((m + k : ℕ) : ℝ)] A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source and role. This is Simon, Ch. 2, proof of Theorem 1.9 (chapter-02.txt lines 366–411, printed pp. 45–46), i.e. Steps 4–7 of the parent proof. It is specialised to Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measures (all normalizing constants c_s = 1). Simon's use of the isodiametric inequality (lines 401–406) is replaced by the sibling lemma volume_diameter_bound, so the constant is ωₘ := λₘ(B₁(0)) instead of ωₘω_k/ω_{m+k}. The hypothesis μH[m+k](A) < ∞ is Simon's hypothesis H^{m+k}(A) < ∞. As in the parent (its Remark (i)), measurability of A is not used. Instead of Simon's upper integral and monotone limit (Remark 1.10, lines 407–411), the parent's Step 7 (liminf and Fatou) is used, which directly produces the required Borel majorant g.

Notation. diam = extended diameter in [0, ∞]. For a set T and real s, cost_s(T) := diam(T)^s if T ≠ ∅ and cost_s(∅) := 0; this is the cost used by Mathlib's Hausdorff measure (⨆ _ : T.Nonempty, …). For n ∈ ℕ and x ∈ [0, ∞], the real power x^{(n:ℝ)} equals the ordinary power xⁿ, so x^k·x^m = x^{m+k} for every x ∈ [0, ∞], including 0 and ∞. λₘ = volume on ℝᵐ. ω := ωₘ = λₘ(B₁(0)) < ∞, because B₁(0) is bounded in the finite-dimensional space ℝᵐ. For i ∈ ℕ put ρᵢ := 1/i ∈ (0, ∞] (ρ₀ = ∞); then ρᵢ > 0, ρᵢ ≠ 0 and ρᵢ → 0.

Proof.
1. Covers (Simon (1), lines 366–370; parent Step 4). For each i, apply the sibling lemma hausdorff_near_optimal_cover with X = ℝ^N, d = m + k, s = A and r = ε = ρᵢ, using μH[m+k](A) < ∞. Choosing such a cover for every i (countable choice) gives sets C_{ij} ⊆ ℝ^N (i, j ∈ ℕ) with
 (1a) A ⊆ ⋃ⱼ C_{ij};
 (1b) diam C_{ij} ≤ ρᵢ for all j;
 (1c) Σⱼ cost_{m+k}(C_{ij}) ≤ μH[m+k](A) + ρᵢ.
2. The functions gᵢ and g (Simon lines 371–377; parent Step 4). Let K_{ij} := closure of f(C_{ij}), a closed and hence Borel subset of ℝᵐ. For y ∈ ℝᵐ set
 gᵢ(y) := Σⱼ diam(C_{ij})^k · 1_{K_{ij}}(y) ∈ [0, ∞],  g(y) := liminf_{i→∞} gᵢ(y).
 Each summand y ↦ diam(C_{ij})^k·1_{K_{ij}}(y) is a constant times the indicator of a Borel set, hence Borel. A countable sum of Borel [0, ∞]-valued functions is Borel, so every gᵢ is Borel. The liminf of a sequence of Borel [0, ∞]-valued functions is Borel, so g is Borel. This is the required measurability.
3. Pointwise bound (Simon (2), lines 377–384; parent Steps 5 and 7). Fix y ∈ ℝᵐ and put S := A ∩ f⁻¹{y}. For each i let Jᵢ := {j ∈ ℕ : y ∈ f(C_{ij})}, a countable set; each C_{ij} with j ∈ Jᵢ is nonempty.
 (3a) Cover: S ⊆ ⋃_{j∈Jᵢ} C_{ij}. If x ∈ S then x ∈ A, so x ∈ C_{ij} for some j by (1a); then y = f(x) ∈ f(C_{ij}), i.e. j ∈ Jᵢ.
 (3b) Liminf bound: μH[k](S) ≤ liminf_i Σ_{j∈Jᵢ} diam(C_{ij})^k. By definition μH[k](S) = sup_{ρ>0} I_ρ(S), where I_ρ(S) is the infimum of Σ cost_k over countable covers of S by sets of diameter ≤ ρ. Fix ρ > 0 and choose i₀ with ρᵢ ≤ ρ for all i ≥ i₀ (possible since ρᵢ → 0). For i ≥ i₀, the family (C_{ij})_{j∈Jᵢ} covers S by (3a) and consists of sets of diameter ≤ ρ by (1b). Enumerate it as a sequence, padding with empty sets of cost 0 if Jᵢ is finite; if Jᵢ = ∅ then S = ∅ and the all-empty cover has cost 0. Since cost_k(T) ≤ diam(T)^k for every T, I_ρ(S) ≤ Σ_{j∈Jᵢ} diam(C_{ij})^k for all i ≥ i₀, hence I_ρ(S) ≤ liminf_i Σ_{j∈Jᵢ} diam(C_{ij})^k. Now take the supremum over ρ > 0. (Mathlib packages exactly this as MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum, applied with the countable index types ιᵢ := {j : ℕ // y ∈ f '' C i j}, the sets t i j := C i j, the radii r i := ρᵢ → 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero), the diameter bound (1b) and the cover (3a).)
 (3c) Comparison with gᵢ: for every i, Σ_{j∈Jᵢ} diam(C_{ij})^k ≤ gᵢ(y). Write the left side as Σⱼ 1_{Jᵢ}(j)·diam(C_{ij})^k and compare termwise. If j ∈ Jᵢ then y ∈ f(C_{ij}) ⊆ K_{ij}, so the j-th term of gᵢ(y) is also diam(C_{ij})^k. If j ∉ Jᵢ the left term is 0.
 (3d) By (3b), (3c) and monotonicity of liminf: μH[k](S) ≤ liminf_i Σ_{j∈Jᵢ} diam(C_{ij})^k ≤ liminf_i gᵢ(y) = g(y).
4. Integral of gᵢ (Simon lines 385–406; parent Step 6). Fix i. Integrals and countable sums of nonnegative measurable functions commute (monotone convergence), and ∫ c·1_K dλₘ = c·λₘ(K) for Borel K. Hence
 ∫ gᵢ dλₘ = Σⱼ diam(C_{ij})^k · λₘ(K_{ij}).
 Each term is at most ω·L^m·cost_{m+k}(C_{ij}):
 (4a) If C_{ij} = ∅: f(C_{ij}) = K_{ij} = ∅, the term is diam(∅)^k·0 = 0 (also for k = 0), and the bound reads 0 ≤ 0.
 (4b) If C_{ij} ≠ ∅: by the sibling lemma volume_diameter_bound applied to f(C_{ij}) ⊆ ℝᵐ, λₘ(K_{ij}) ≤ ω·diam(f(C_{ij}))^m. Since f is L-Lipschitz, diam f(C_{ij}) ≤ L·diam C_{ij} in [0, ∞] (Mathlib: LipschitzWith.ediam_image_le). Multiplication and the m-th power are monotone on [0, ∞], so
 diam(C_{ij})^k·λₘ(K_{ij}) ≤ diam(C_{ij})^k·ω·(L·diam C_{ij})^m = ω·L^m·diam(C_{ij})^{m+k} = ω·L^m·cost_{m+k}(C_{ij}).
 The middle equality is commutative-semiring arithmetic in [0, ∞]: (ab)^m = a^m b^m and x^k x^m = x^{m+k}.
 Summing over j, pulling out the constant and using (1c):
 ∫ gᵢ dλₘ ≤ ω·L^m·Σⱼ cost_{m+k}(C_{ij}) ≤ ω·L^m·(μH[m+k](A) + ρᵢ).
5. Fatou and the limit (Simon lines 407–411 and Remark 1.10; parent Step 7). By Fatou's lemma for the Borel functions gᵢ ≥ 0, then step 4 and monotonicity of liminf:
 ∫ g dλₘ = ∫ liminf_i gᵢ dλₘ ≤ liminf_i ∫ gᵢ dλₘ ≤ liminf_i ω·L^m·(μH[m+k](A) + ρᵢ).
 Since ρᵢ → 0, μH[m+k](A) + ρᵢ → μH[m+k](A) in [0, ∞]. The constant ω·L^m is finite (ω < ∞ and L < ∞), so multiplying by it is continuous on [0, ∞]. Hence ω·L^m·(μH[m+k](A) + ρᵢ) → ω·L^m·μH[m+k](A), and the liminf of a convergent sequence is its limit. Therefore ∫ g dλₘ ≤ ωₘ·L^m·μH[m+k](A).
6. Conclusion. g is Borel (step 2), satisfies μH[k](A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g(y) for every y (step 3), and satisfies the integral bound (step 5). ∎

Edge cases. The uniform argument covers all of them, with no case split.
- m = 0: ℝ⁰ is a point, and volume_diameter_bound holds for m = 0 with (·)⁰ = 1.
- k = 0: μH[0] counts points. In (3b) the sets C_{ij} with j ∈ Jᵢ are nonempty, and in (4a) the indicator removes the empty C_{ij}, so the convention 0⁰ = 1 never matters.
- L = 0: volume_diameter_bound and the Lipschitz bound hold verbatim, with the [0, ∞] convention 0·∞ = 0.
- i = 0: ρ₀ = ∞; all inequalities above remain valid in [0, ∞], and single indices do not affect a liminf.

  have hA := @Submission.hausdorffMeasure_exists_cover_tsum_le_add
  have hB := Submission.volume_closure_le_unitBall_mul_ediam_pow
  intro N m k A f L hf hA_fin
  set ω := volume (Metric.ball (0 : Rn m) 1) with hω
  have hω_top : ω ≠ ∞ := measure_ball_ne_top
  have hcov : ∀ i : ℕ, ∃ t : ℕ → Set (Rn N), A ⊆ ⋃ j, t j ∧ (∀ j, Metric.ediam (t j) ≤ (i : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹) ∧ ∑' j, ⨆ _ : (t j).Nonempty, Metric.ediam (t j) ^ ((m + k : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ μH[((m + k : ℕ) : ℝ)] A + (i : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ := fun i =>
    hA _ A _ _ (ENNReal.inv_pos.2 (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top i)) (ENNReal.inv_ne_zero.2 (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top i)) hA_fin
  choose C hCcov hCdiam hCsum using hcov
  set G : ℕ → Rn m → ℝ≥0∞ := fun i y => ∑' j, (closure (f '' C i j)).indicator (fun _ => Metric.ediam (C i j) ^ (k : ℝ)) y with hG
  have hGmeas : ∀ i, Measurable (G i) := fun i =>
    Measurable.ennreal_tsum fun j => measurable_const.indicator isClosed_closure.measurableSet
  refine ⟨fun y => liminf (fun i => G i y) atTop, Measurable.liminf hGmeas, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro y
    have hcover : ∀ᶠ i in atTop, A ∩ f ⁻¹' {y} ⊆ ⋃ j : {j : ℕ // y ∈ f '' C i j}, C i j.1 :=

    refine h1.trans (liminf_le_liminf (Eventually.of_forall fun i => ?_))

      _ ≤ G i y := ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum fun j => by

proof_key_steps: For each i apply hausdorff_near_optimal_cover (d = m+k, r = ε = 1/i) to get covers C_{ij} of A with diam ≤ 1/i and Σⱼ cost_{m+k}(C_{ij}) ≤ μH[m+k](A) + 1/i.
Define the Borel functions gᵢ := Σⱼ diam(C_{ij})^k·1_{closure f(C_{ij})} and g := liminf gᵢ, which is Borel.
Pointwise: A ∩ f⁻¹{y} is covered by the C_{ij} with y ∈ f(C_{ij}), so μH[k](A ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ liminf_i Σ_{j : y ∈ f(C_{ij})} diam(C_{ij})^k ≤ liminf gᵢ(y) = g(y) (hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum).
Integral: ∫gᵢ = Σⱼ diam(C_{ij})^k·λₘ(closure f(C_{ij})) ≤ ωₘL^m·Σⱼ cost_{m+k}(C_{ij}) ≤ ωₘL^m(μH[m+k](A) + 1/i), by volume_diameter_bound and diam f(C) ≤ L·diam C.
